newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Horse racing-Roche wins Guineas and Derby Trials.
newsitem.headline: Horse racing-Roche wins Guineas and Derby Trials.

text.p: Ireland's veteran jockey Christy Roche was the star of the show as he rode five winners, including the winners of the Listed Irish 1,000 Guineas and Group Three Irish Derby Trial races, at Leopardstown on Sunday.

Roche, 47, came with a storming late finish on board Charles O'Brien-trained Ashley Park (8-1) to land the Irish Derby Trial Stakes run over one-and-a-quarter miles (2-km) by a short-head at the posts from Dermot Weld's Casey Tibbs (9-4).
John Oxx-trained Ebadiyla (2-1 favourite) finished a further short-head adrift in third spot.
"I thought he'd win. I really fancied him," Roche said. "He could have won by two lengths on the day. About two furlongs out I found myself boxed in and had to take a hard pull."
Charles O'Brien, a son of legendary Irish trainer, Vincent O'Brien, said Ashley Park would have one more run before the Irish Derby at The Curragh on June 29.
The winning trainer said that his other stable-star Olympic Majesty would run at Mallow racecourse in Cork on May 17 before going for the French Derby.
Roche had earlier guided Aidan O'Brien's 5-2 on-favourite Strawberry Roan to a three-and-a-half length triumph in the Irish 1,000 Guineas Trial over one mile (1.6-km).
O'Brien said Strawberry Roan, along with stable-mate Classic Park, would now go for the Irish 1,000 Guineas proper at The Curragh on May 24.

Roche and Aidan O'Brien also combined to win the European Breeders Fund Race over five furlongs (1-km) with Sideman who will go for the Coventry Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Killiney Handicap over six furlongs (1.2-km) with Air of Distinction.
The Roche-Charles O'Brien partnership produced Dr.Johnson to win the Anglo Printers Maiden over one-and-a-half miles (2.4- km).
